items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: From then on, Louis Armstrong was my dominant influence

ctx.x: Bill Davison was born in a place called Defiance, Ohio, and was known as "Wild Bill" because he was able to drink a large quantity of alchohol at a very young age and I suppose he did some wild things as most young men do under the influence of alchohol.

At that time, even though he was two years younger than I was, he was blowing a whole lot more trumpet than me. I was able to read fairly well, but I was not too well educated in different keys. My range was not more than high 'C'. Probably I could have changed that by using different mouth pieces but I didn't get to know about things like that until I met Louis Armstrong later on. Even so, high notes never really bothered me, I had a good enough range for the time although I was not as gifted as players like…

One week after the visit of "Wild Bill" and his friend, they came back to Woodlawn Inn and Bill wanted to play my horn again, but he was so drunk that he could hardly stand. I let him blow my horn but he really didn't play anything that night and I had my revenge because I blew him out. His friend came to get him and put him in a back room where he immediately went to sleep.

items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I went backstage after the show to say hello to them... I asked Pops for a photo. He said 'Sure, Gate, I'll give you one.'

ctx.x: A few months after I had returned to the USA, Louis Armstrong was playing a week at the Roxy Theatre downtown on the 7th Avenue and 50th Street; and I went down to catch the show. Pops had taken over the Luis Russell orchestra and as I knew all the musicians, I went backstage after the show to say hello to them. I had seen Pops plenty of times, and he had a photo with him, Zilner Randolph and myself that was taken in Cincinnati in 1935 when I was a fugitive from the New York domestic court.

But I wanted an autographed photo of Gate so Higginbottom took me to Louis' dressing room and I asked Pops for a photo. He said 'Sure, Gate, I'll give you one. What's your name?' I told him Bill Coleman.
In August, Benny accepted a job in a dance hall at Coney Island, an amusement park in Long Island, New York, a suburb of New York City, and we played a month there.
